section_summary: This section covers diplomatic correspondence, SCAP directives, and administrative memoranda from 1945 to 1949 regarding the implementation of Japan's post-World War II agrarian land reform and its application to foreign nationals, absentee owners abroad, and dual Japanese-American citizens. It details SCAP policies governing property exemptions, diplomatic notifications coordinated with Latin American and North American governments, and controversies over church and Axis holdings. Additionally, it includes SCAP's restitution of impounded personal property to former Philippine puppet government officials and a comprehensive sociological survey assessing Japanese farmers' attitudes toward rural economic problems and land reform.

subfiles.about: A comprehensive sociological survey of 1,300 farm household heads across thirteen Japanese villages examining land reform, economic anxieties, taxes, and rural institutions.
subfiles.from: Public Opinion and Sociological Research Division, Civil Information and Education Section and Natural Resources Section, GHQ SCAP
keywords: Attitudes of Farmers Toward Rural Problems
subfiles.summary: This preliminary report presents the findings of a late 1948 survey of 1,300 farm household heads across thirteen representative villages in Japan conducted by Dr. Arthur F. Raper with SCAP's Civil Information and Education Section and Natural Resources Section. The survey reveals that while a solid majority of farmers—particularly former tenants—viewed the land reform program as beneficial to their households and communities, widespread pessimism prevailed regarding deteriorating economic conditions, burdensome income taxes, grain delivery quotas, and the threat of an impending depression.
subfiles.title: Report: Attitudes of Farmers Toward Rural Problems
subfiles.to: SCAP Staff Sections, Eighth Army Military Government, and Department of State
